preamble.summary: The death of the firstborn retold as the descent of God's all-powerful Word from heaven. Israel protected by the Passover while Egypt's children die. Aaron halts a later plague through intercession.
preamble.remarkable: Verse 15-16 ('Your all-powerful Word leaped from heaven, from the royal throne, a fierce warrior into the midst of a land of destruction') became one of the most important Christological texts in Western liturgy — the Introit for the Sunday within the Octave of Christmas. The personified Logos as divine warrior shaped medieval Christology.
preamble.friction: The boundary between personified 'Word' and the later Johannine Logos theology is delicate — the Latin omnipotens sermo tuus bridges wisdom literature and Christology in ways the author may not have intended.
preamble.connections: John 1:1-14 (the Word), Revelation 19:11-16 (warrior from heaven), Exodus 12 (Passover), Hebrews 4:12 (living word as sword). The Christmas liturgy 'Dum medium silentium' derives from vv. 14-15.

verses.text_latin: Sanctis autem tuis maxima erat lux et horum quidem vocem audiebant sed figuram non videbant
verses.rendering: But for your holy ones there was very great light. Their enemies heard their voices but could not see their forms,
translator_notes: Direct contrast with ch 17 — the same night that imprisoned Egypt gave Israel light.

verses.text_latin: et quia non et ipsi eadem passi erant glorificabant te et qui ante laesi erant quia non laedebantur gratias agebant
verses.rendering: and they counted them blessed because they had not suffered the same things, and gave thanks that those previously wronged were not now harming them, and asked pardon for having been at enmity.

verses.text_latin: Pro quibus igneam columnam ducem habuerunt ignotae viae et solem sine laesura boni hospitii praestitisti
verses.rendering: Instead of the darkness you provided a pillar of blazing fire as guide on an unknown journey, and a harmless sun for their glorious wandering.
translator_notes: The pillar of fire is a 'sun' that does not harm — contrasting Egypt's harmful darkness.

key_terms.note: Exodus 13:21 retold through Wisdom's theological lens

verses.text_latin: Digni quidem illi carere luce et pati carcerem tenebrarum qui inclusos custodiebant filios tuos per quos incipiebat incorruptum legis lumen saeculo dari
verses.rendering: For the Egyptians deserved to be deprived of light and imprisoned in darkness — they who had kept your children confined, through whom the imperishable light of the Law was to be given to the world.
translator_notes: Incorruptum legis lumen (imperishable light of the Law) — Torah as cosmic light, given through Israel to the world.

key_terms.note: Torah theology: the Law is eternal light destined for all humanity, not merely Israel's possession

verses.text_latin: Cum cogitarent iustorum occidere infantes et uno exposito filio et liberato in traductionem illorum multitudinem filiorum abstulisti et pariter illos perdidisti in aqua valida
verses.rendering: When they resolved to kill the infants of the righteous — and one child had been exposed and rescued — as punishment you took away the multitude of their own children, and destroyed them all together in the mighty water.
translator_notes: The 'one exposed child' is Moses; the 'mighty water' is the Red Sea. Measure-for-measure theology.

verses.text_latin: Illa enim nox ante cognita est a patribus nostris ut vere scientes quibus iuramentis crediderunt animaequiores essent
verses.rendering: That night was made known beforehand to our ancestors, so that having sure knowledge of the oaths they trusted, they might be of good courage.

verses.text_latin: Suscepta est autem a populo tuo sanitas quidem iustorum iniustorum autem exterminatio
verses.rendering: Your people received both the salvation of the righteous and the destruction of their enemies.

verses.text_latin: Sicut enim laesisti adversarios sic et nos provocans magnificasti
verses.rendering: For as you punished our adversaries, so you glorified us whom you had called.

verses.text_latin: Absconse enim sacrificabant iusti pueri bonorum et iustitiae legem in concordia disposuerunt similiter et bona et mala recepturos se sanctos secundum quod iam patrum decantabant laudes
verses.rendering: For the righteous children of the good were offering sacrifice in secret, and with one accord they established the divine law that the saints would share alike in the same blessings and dangers, the ancestors already singing the hymns of praise.
translator_notes: Reference to the first Passover — families in secret, singing while Egypt's firstborn die.

verses.text_latin: Resonabat autem inconveniens inimicorum vox et flebilis audiebatur planctus ploratorum infantium
verses.rendering: But there resounded in dissonance the cry of enemies, and a pitiful wailing was heard for children being mourned.

verses.text_latin: Simili autem poena servus cum domino adflictus est et popularis homo regi similia passus
verses.rendering: Slave and master were punished with the same penalty, and the common person suffered the same as the king.
translator_notes: Death as the great equalizer — a theme that will recur in medieval danse macabre tradition.

verses.text_latin: Similiter ergo omnes uno nomine mortis mortuos habebant innumerabiles nec enim ad sepeliendum vivi sufficiebant quoniam uno momento quae erat praeclarior natio illorum exterminata est
verses.rendering: All alike had innumerable dead, by the one name of death. The living were not even sufficient to bury them, for in a single moment their most distinguished offspring was destroyed.

verses.text_latin: De omnibus enim non credentes propter veneficia tunc vero primum cum fuit exterminium primogenitorum spoponderunt populum Dei esse
verses.rendering: For though they had disbelieved everything because of the sorcerers' enchantments, when the firstborn were destroyed they acknowledged that this people was God's.

verses.text_latin: Cum enim quietum silentium contineret omnia et nox in suo cursu medium iter haberet
verses.rendering: For while gentle silence enveloped all things, and night in its swift course was now half gone,
translator_notes: Dum medium silentium — this verse and the next became the Christmas Introit in the Roman liturgy, applied to Christ's Incarnation. One of the most liturgically important verses in all deuterocanonical literature.

key_terms.note: The cosmic silence before God acts — became the liturgical frame for the Incarnation in Western Christmas worship

verses.text_latin: omnipotens sermo tuus de caelo a regalibus sedibus durus debellator in mediam exterminii terram prosilivit
verses.rendering: your all-powerful Word leaped from heaven, from the royal throne — a fierce warrior into the midst of a land devoted to destruction.
translator_notes: Omnipotens sermo tuus (your all-powerful Word) — the personified divine Word as warrior descending from heaven. In Christian liturgical reading, this became a type of the Incarnation: the Word leaping from God's throne into the world. The Christmas Introit 'Dum medium silentium tenerent omnia' applies this passage to Christ's birth.

key_terms.note: The Logos as divine warrior — bridges OT wisdom theology and NT Johannine Christology. Central to Western Christmas liturgy.

verses.text_latin: Gladium acutum insimulatum imperium tuum portans et stans replevit omnia morte et usque ad caelum attingebat stans in terra
verses.rendering: Bearing your unfeigned commandment as a sharp sword, and standing, it filled all things with death, and while standing on earth it touched the heavens.
translator_notes: The Word stands between heaven and earth, filling creation — an image of cosmic reach. Connects to Revelation 19:15 (sharp sword from his mouth).

key_terms.note: The sword-Word image: Hebrews 4:12, Revelation 1:16, 19:15 all echo this conception

verses.text_latin: Tunc continuo visus somniorum malorum turbaverunt illos et timores supervenerunt insperati
verses.rendering: Then immediately terrible dreams disturbed them, and unexpected fears came upon them.

verses.text_latin: Et alius alibi proiectus semivivus propter quam moriebatur causam demonstrabat mortis
verses.rendering: And one thrown here, another there, half dead, made plain the cause of their death.

verses.text_latin: Visiones enim quae illos turbaverunt haec praemonebant ne inscii quare mala patiebantur perirent
verses.rendering: For the visions that disturbed them forewarned them of this, so that they might not perish without knowing why they suffered.

verses.text_latin: Tetigit autem tunc et iustos temptatio mortis et commotio in eremo facta est multitudinis sed non diu permansit ira tua
verses.rendering: The experience of death touched the righteous also, and a plague struck the multitude in the wilderness, but your wrath did not long continue.
translator_notes: Shifts to Numbers 16-17 — Korah's rebellion and the plague. Even Israel was touched, but briefly.

verses.text_latin: Properans enim homo sine querella deprecari pro populis proferens servitutis suae scutum orationem et per incensum deprecationem adlegans restitit irae et finem inposuit necessitati ostendens quoniam tuus est famulus
verses.rendering: For a blameless man hurried to be their champion; bringing the shield of his ministry — prayer and the propitiation of incense — he withstood your anger and put an end to the disaster, showing that he was your servant.
translator_notes: Aaron with the censer (Numbers 16:47-48) standing between the living and dead — became a priestly type in Catholic theology.

key_terms.note: Aaron's incense as intercessory propitiation — foundational for Catholic priestly mediation theology

verses.text_latin: Vicit autem turbas non in virtute corporis nec armaturae potentia sed verbo illum qui se vexabat subiecit iuramenta parentum et testamentum commemorans
verses.rendering: He overcame the destroyer not by bodily strength nor by force of arms, but by his word he subdued the punisher, appealing to the oaths and covenants made with the ancestors.

verses.text_latin: Cum enim iam acervatim cecidissent super alterutrum mortui interstitit et amputavit impetum et divisit illam quae ad vivos ducebat viam
verses.rendering: For when the dead had already fallen in heaps upon one another, he interposed and cut off the onslaught, and barred the way that led to the living.

verses.text_latin: In veste enim poderis quam habebat totus erat orbis terrarum et parentum magnalia in quattuor ordinibus lapidum erant sculpta et magnificentia tua in diademate capitis illius sculpta erat
verses.rendering: For on his full-length robe the whole world was represented, and the glories of the ancestors were engraved on the four rows of stones, and your majesty was on the diadem upon his head.
translator_notes: The high priest's vestments as cosmic symbol — the ephod stones represent all Israel, the robe represents creation. Philo and Josephus elaborate this cosmic priestly symbolism.

key_terms.note: Greek poderes — the high priestly robe reaching to the feet, representing cosmic mediation

verses.text_latin: His enim cessit qui exterminabat et haec extimuit non enim erat sola temptatio irae sufficiens
verses.rendering: To these things the destroyer yielded, and these he feared; for the mere experience of wrath was sufficient.
translator_notes: The destroyer (exterminans) yields to priestly intercession — the power of liturgical mediation over divine wrath.
